fixes.explanation: A tower is a fair guess, since it also goes up high. But the dream isn't about one. The text says it was "…a ladder that rested on the earth with its top reaching up to heaven…" (Gen 28:12) A tower you walk around and admire. A ladder is one you climb, and it's the one Jacob sees.

Noah's a big name, baker, but he's not in this blessing. Isaac says, "And may He give the blessing of Abraham to you and your descendants…" (Gen 28:4) The name in the verse is Abraham, and he's Isaac's own father (Gen 25:19). The blessing stays in the family, handed straight down from Isaac's own father.

The dream shows "…God’s angels were going up and down the ladder." (Gen 28:12) Up AND down, baker. Jacob is lying there with a stone under his head (Gen 28:11), and the dream has angels moving on a ladder that rests on the earth and reaches to heaven.

Jacob put a stone under his head, not his head on the ground. The passage also does not say whether anyone was waiting at the bottom of the ladder.
